title: Unified fetch primitives: cursor semantics, resumable streams, and graceful client downgrade
creator: Ava Chen
description: This PRD defines a cross-language client contract for fetch primitives used by Redwood SDKs: strong cursor pagination, resumable streaming iterators, and downgrade-safe behaviors for older clients. The goal is to provide a single, well-specified surface that SDKs (Python/TS/Go) can implement while preserving backwards compatibility for existing consumers. We want clear failure/retry semantics, an opaque cursor format with compatibility guarantees, and a resumable streaming API that can survive transient infra restarts or route failovers.
requirements: REQ-01: Cursor pagination must use an opaque base64 token; server must accept tokens issued by prior runtime versions for at least 12 months.
REQ-02: All SDKs must expose a consistent iterator abstraction: `paged_iter()` (pull) and `stream_iterator()` (push/streaming) with resume/checkpoint APIs.

REQ-03: Resume for streams must support two modes: (a) offset-based resume for idempotent sequences (sequence_id + offset), (b) state-checkpoint resume for non-idempotent outputs using checkpoint tokens.

REQ-04: Retry semantics: transient errors (5xx, network) must be automatically retried with exponential backoff and jitter; client should surface retry metadata for observability and allow override policies.

REQ-05: Downgrade safety: when clients call new parameters or new response fields, server must provide stable defaults and feature-gates so older clients receive compatible payloads and error codes when a feature is unsupported.

REQ-06: Streaming timeouts and reconnection: servers will emit stream heartbeats and checkpoints every N messages (configurable) to enable clients to rejoin without data loss up to a configurable retention window (default 5 minutes).
nonfunctional_requirements: Latency: adding resumability metadata must not increase median response generation latency by more than 5% on typical workloads. Token-size: cursors must be <4KB. SDK ergonomics: Python/TS/Go idioms must be preserved (async iterator for Python/TS, channel-like consumer for Go).
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: Implementations in Python/TS/Go expose the documented APIs and pass the cross-language test harness (pagination unit tests + streaming resume scenarios).
AC-02: Server accepts historic cursor tokens from two previous minor releases in test harness and preserves ordering semantics for paged results.

AC-03: Simulated transient infra restart test shows stream resume recovers to the last checkpoint with no duplicate delivery for idempotent sequences and with explicit deduplication guidance for non-idempotent sequences.
AC-04: SDK docs and migration guide created, including a clear compatibility matrix and a decision tree for when to use offset vs checkpoint resume.
AC-05: Performance regression is measured: mean latency increase <5% and additional token cost <1% for standard eval prompts.
AC-06: PM/Eng/Design sign-off on API ergonomics and changelog for the public SDKs.
AC-07: Demo: integrate TypeScript SDK streaming resume into a small Redwood demo app and record a runbook showing restore after simulated failover.
api_contract_examples:
Python example (async iterator, resumable):
async for item in client.paged_iter(endpoint='responses', page_size=100, cursor=None):
    process(item)
# resume with cursor token
async for item in client.paged_iter(endpoint='responses', page_size=100, cursor=last_cursor):
    process(item)

Python streaming (checkpoint resume):
async def consume():
    stream = client.stream_iterator('live_responses', checkpoint_interval=200)
    async for event in stream:
        if event.type == 'checkpoint':
            save_checkpoint_token(event.token)
        handle(event)
# resume
stream = client.stream_iterator('live_responses', resume_token=load_checkpoint_token())

Server contract: cursors are opaque base64 JSON blobs with fields {v:int, t:string, payload:object}. Servers must validate version v and map t to routing metadata; unknown fields must be ignored by newer servers to keep forward compatibility.
scope: MVP covers paged pull iterators and streaming with checkpoint resume. Out of scope for MVP: automatic server-side compaction of checkpoint tokens and multi-tenant cross-shard cursor merge; these are follow-ons.
scope_changes: 2025-02-12: Removed initial plan for server-side durable replay buffer (ENG requested re-scope due to infra complexity). Kept checkpoint tokens instead for client-driven resume.
2025-02-15: Narrowed streaming retention window to configurable default 5 minutes (was 30 minutes) to limit storage cost; added acceptance criterion for configurable retention.
decisions: DEC-01: Use opaque base64 cursor containing a small JSON envelope rather than a fully-opaque binary token to ease debugging while remaining opaque to clients.
DEC-02: Two resume modes (offset vs checkpoint) chosen to balance simplicity for idempotent streams and safety for non-idempotent outputs (e.g., user-visible side-effects).
DEC-03: Retry policy will be client-configurable with a sensible default (max_retries=5, base=200ms, max_backoff=5s, jitter=true).
tradeoffs: T-01: Opaque JSON cursors improve troubleshooting but increase token size slightly; we limit payloads to 4KB to control client-side memory.
T-02: Shorter stream retention reduces storage cost and lowers ability to rejoin long-outage clients; mitigation: recommend server-side bookmarks for long-tail consumers and document best practices.
T-03: Adding resumability requires server-side checkpoints which add CPU IO; tradeoff accepted for higher reliability of streaming UX.
